title: Scaling the Add-On Down Payment by Invoices Already Enrolled
content:
Patient Services Academy — training note on **Patient Payment Plans**: how the number of invoices a plan already carries scales the add-on down payment owed on a further invoice.

## The rule

The add-on down payment is also scaled by the number of invoices the plan already carries: by one and a half when 3 or more invoices have been enrolled on the plan, by one and a quarter when exactly 2 have, and not at all when one has.

The number is read from the plan ledger: each invoice enrollment line the plan already carries counts once. The invoice being added is not one of them.

| Invoices already enrolled on the plan | Scale |
|---|---|
| 1 | Not scaled (a multiplier of 1) |
| Exactly 2 | One and a quarter (a multiplier of 1.25) |
| 3 or more | One and a half (a multiplier of 1.5) |

The scale is a multiplier inside the product that forms the add-on down payment: the balance due on the invoice being added is multiplied, all together, by the plan's down-payment percentage, by any raise or other scale that applies, and by this scale; that single product is rounded to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up, and only then is it compared with the add-on minimum. The scale never multiplies an amount already rounded, nor the add-on minimum.

## Questions answered

**A plan opened with a single invoice; the patient now adds a second. Is the add-on down payment scaled?** No. The plan carries one invoice, so it is not scaled.

**A plan carries 2 invoices and a third is being added. What scale applies?** One and a quarter.

**A plan has had 4 invoices enrolled, one of them since paid in full. What scale applies to a fifth?** The plan ledger shows 4 enrollment lines, which is 3 or more: one and a half.

**Hypothetical figures (down-payment percentage 10; no raise and no other scale).** An invoice with a balance due of 360.00 gives a product of 36.00 on a plan carrying one invoice, 360.00 by 10 percent by 1.25, that is 45.00, on a plan carrying exactly 2, and 360.00 by 10 percent by 1.5, that is 54.00, on a plan carrying 3 or more. An invoice with a balance due of 160.00 on a plan carrying 3 invoices gives 160.00 by 10 percent by 1.5, that is 24.00; where the add-on minimum is 25.00, the add-on down payment is 25.00, the minimum itself not being scaled.
